stories.headline: Catastrophic Glacial Flood Kills 939 People Along Nepal-Tibet Border
stories.body: Nepalese disaster authorities said a flood on the Nepal-Tibet border killed 939 people [c3]. Officials estimate that 3,925 people are missing across the area [c4]. That total includes 592 foreign nationals [c4]. Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah said rescuers saved 279 people from hydropower plant sites [c5]. Shah added that 11,379 people were saved across the country [c6]. Rescuers used explosives to blast into a hillside on Monday [c2]. They pumped air into the Trishuli-3A site to reach trapped workers [c2]. An international team with military personnel from China and Nepal is searching for trapped workers [c7]. Experts from India, Korea, and Australia joined the rescue team [c7]. In Chitwan district, rivers brought nearly 300 dead bodies to the banks [c8]. Local people carried out makeshift temporary burials [c8]. Chinese state media reported 16 dead and 546 missing in Tibet [c9]. Chinese authorities penalised people who speculated online that Tibet's casualties were higher [c10]. Nepalese researchers found an ice-rock avalanche triggered the August 26 flood [c14]. The avalanche travelled 22 kilometres in just over seven minutes [c14]. It moved at an average speed of 167 kilometres per hour [c14]. The flood affected 13 hydropower projects and one solar project [c17]. It knocked 431 megawatts of power generation capacity offline [c17].

vocab.meaning: to save something from being destroyed or lost
broken pieces or rubbish left after a destruction
a person killed or injured in a disaster or war

stories.headline: US and Iran Exchange Military Strikes Near Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
US military forces launched strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on Sunday [c19]. The United States acted to prevent Iran from putting mines in the Strait of Hormuz [c19]. US President Donald Trump said that his country was going to hit Iran hard [c18]. Iranian state media said three people died in the US attack on Larak Island [c20]. The report added that several other people were wounded [c20]. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps gave a different casualty figure [c30]. The Revolutionary Guard said two people died on Larak Island [c30]. It said two other people were injured in the strike [c30]. Iran requires commercial tankers that pass Larak Island to undergo checks [c31]. Reports say Iran charges 2 million dollars for each vessel crossing [c31].

Iran's Revolutionary Guards responded by launching ballistic missiles [c21]. They targeted two American military bases located in Jordan [c21]. The Revolutionary Guards claimed the missile strikes caused heavy damage to the bases [c21]. The United Arab Emirates foreign ministry reported military activity in the region [c27]. The ministry said UAE forces intercepted an Iranian drone over territorial waters [c27]. The UAE condemned the drone action as a dangerous escalation [c27].

Iranian state television claimed that a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz [c28]. US Central Command denied that claim [c28]. American military officials said no supertanker struck mines in the waterway [c28].

The military conflict began on February 28, 2026 [c29]. The United States and Israel started the conflict by launching wide-ranging strikes on Iran [c32]. Trump wrote a post on Truth Social about Kharg Island [c25]. Trump called Iran a failed nation [c23]. He claimed that the nation is dead [c23]. US Vice President JD Vance explained the social media post [c25]. Vance said Trump wanted to send a signal to Iran about Kharg Island [c25]. A US official confirmed that American forces did not hit Kharg Island overnight [c26]. Before the conflict started on February 28, Kharg Island handled about 90 percent of Iranian oil exports [c29].

Iranian leaders called for peace during a summit in Kyrgyzstan [c22]. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian urged all sides to start a dialogue [c22]. Pezeshkian said that continuing the war helps neither Iran nor the wider region [c22]. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also spoke on Iranian state television [c24]. Araghchi demanded that the United States return to its previous commitments [c24].

vocab.meaning: stopped or caught something before it reached its destination
an increase in the intensity or seriousness of a conflict

stories.headline: Lionel Messi Retires From International Soccer With Argentina
stories.body: Argentine soccer star Lionel Messi retired from international football on Monday, August 31, 2026 [c33]. Messi ended his international career at age 39 after 21 years of national-team duty [c36]. He played 207 games for Argentina [c37]. Messi scored 125 goals for his country, making him Argentina's all-time top scorer [c37]. 21 of those goals came during World Cup matches [c37]. Messi won the FIFA World Cup in Qatar in 2022 [c39]. He also won Copa America titles with Argentina in 2021 and 2024 [c39]. In 2023, he won a record eighth Ballon d'Or award [c41]. Messi revealed that he wrote his retirement letter on July 21 [c38]. That was two days after Argentina lost the 2026 World Cup final to Spain [c38]. He delayed publishing the letter because his father had health problems [c38]. In 2012, Messi set a record by scoring 91 goals in a calendar year [c40]. Forbes estimated Messi's total net worth at 1.1 billion dollars in 2026 [c34]. Inter Miami owner Jorge Mas valued Messi's yearly pay between 70 million and 80 million dollars [c35].

vocab.meaning: work or service that someone is expected to do
made known something that was secret

stories.headline: Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin Meet at SCO Summit in Kyrgyzstan
stories.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan [c42]. The two leaders spoke on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit [c42]. The meeting marked the 25th anniversary of the regional group [c43]. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov spoke about the meeting [c44]. Peskov said Xi and Putin mainly discussed economic relations [c44]. He said they touched on the Ukraine conflict only in passing [c44]. Xi said China wants to work with Russia to build an equal and orderly world [c46]. Putin suggested that the two countries cooperate on artificial intelligence and digital innovation [c47]. Putin offered to create a permanent visa-free system for visitors between the nations [c48]. He said China must decide if such an agreement is helpful [c48]. Putin said visa-free travel had already boosted tourism between Russia and China by 43 percent [c49]. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi also met Putin in Bishkek [c45]. Modi said India is willing to help solve the Ukraine conflict [c45].

vocab.meaning: an official meeting between leaders of governments
the creation of new ideas, methods, or products

stories.headline: Narendra Modi Meets Iranian and Russian Leaders at SCO Summit
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on August 31, 2026 [c54]. The leaders held talks on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit [c54]. This was the first top-level meeting between India and Iran since war started on Iran in February 2026 [c55]. Prime Minister Modi urged Pezeshkian to work to ensure peace in West Asia [c56]. Modi asked Iran to protect freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz [c56]. Pezeshkian blamed Israel and the United States for starting the conflict [c57]. Pezeshkian asked Modi to use India's many international contacts to help start talks [c57]. Pezeshkian said Iran remained committed to ceasefire agreements [c58]. He added that the American side failed to meet its promises [c58]. In July 2026, an Indian delegation went to Iran for the funeral of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei [c59]. The delegation included Bihar Governor Syed Ata Hasnain and Minister of State Pabitra Margherita [c59].

Modi also held a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek [c60]. Modi told Putin that Russia should move away from endless war [c60]. Modi said Russia should work towards the end of war [c60]. Modi told Putin that India supports all efforts to end the war in Ukraine [c66]. The two leaders discussed attacks on merchant ships in the Black Sea [c61]. Those attacks killed at least five Indian seafarers [c61]. Modi and Putin rode together in Putin's limousine to the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games [c62]. Putin said trade between Russia and India grew by 2.6 percent in the first half of 2026 [c63]. Putin said almost 40,000 Indian students now study in Russia [c64]. He said that number grew seven times over the past decade [c64]. Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri spoke after the meeting [c65]. Misri said Modi and Putin discussed fixing the growing trade gap between the two countries [c65].

Before the main summit, Modi met Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov [c50]. Modi also met Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan [c50]. Modi and Pashinyan discussed cooperation in defence, medicine, mining, education, trade, and culture [c53]. Modi attended the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan [c51]. Formal talks between Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping did not take place in Bishkek [c52]. Officials moved those bilateral talks to the upcoming BRICS summit in India on September 12 and 13 [c52].

vocab.meaning: a group of people chosen to represent a country or group
the movement of ships or vehicles along a planned route

stories.headline: India Rejects Hague Court Ruling on Indus Waters Treaty
stories.body: India rejected an interim ruling on the Indus Waters Treaty issued by a court in The Hague [c67]. India's Ministry of External Affairs called the Court of Arbitration illegally constituted [c67]. The Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled that the 1960 treaty remains fully in force [c68]. The court said India had no justification to suspend the agreement [c68]. The panel was chaired by Sean D. Murphy from the United States [c79]. The ruling ordered India to limit work on a hydroelectric plant in Jammu and Kashmir [c69]. Specifically, the court stopped India from concreting parts of the Ratle project dam wall [c78]. Pakistan petitioned the court in March 2026 to judge the status of the treaty [c77]. India suspended the treaty in April 2025 after a terror attack in Pahalgam killed 26 people [c71, c76]. A proxy group of Lashkar-e-Taiba carried out that attack [c76]. The 1960 treaty gave India control over the eastern rivers Beas, Ravi, and Sutlej [c72]. It gave Pakistan control over the western rivers Indus, Chenab, and Jhelum [c72]. Since the suspension, India accelerated work on power projects like Ratle and Kishenganga [c73]. A World Bank expert will decide by July 2027 if Indian hydro projects follow the treaty [c74].

vocab.meaning: temporary or meant to last for a short time
a state of temporary disuse or pause

stories.headline: Draft Voter Lists in India Delete Millions of Registered Names
stories.body: Electoral authorities removed 6.15 crore voter names from draft lists across 19 Indian states and territories [c80]. The deletions happened during phase three of the Special Intensive Revision [c80]. Out of 36.08 crore total voters in those areas, officials kept 29.93 crore names on the rolls [c80, c81]. Delhi recorded the highest percentage of deletions at 32.78 percent [c82]. Delhi deleted 47.7 lakh names, dropping its electorate from 1.45 crore to 97.5 lakh [c90]. Maharashtra saw the largest absolute reduction, losing 2.06 crore voter names [c83]. That removed 21.1 percent of Maharashtra's previous voter base, leaving 7.7 crore voters [c87]. Karnataka recorded 1.07 crore voter deletions, which was the second highest total [c84]. Draft rolls also removed over 19 percent of voters in Karnataka, 16 percent in Haryana, and 10.8 percent in Andhra Pradesh [c92]. Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy wrote to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar [c85]. Shivakumar and Reddy raised serious concerns about the huge number of deleted voters [c85]. In March, the Supreme Court upheld the legality of the Special Intensive Revision process [c86].

vocab.meaning: all the people in a country or area who are allowed to vote
the process of re-examining and updating something
